newsitem.title: GERMANY: German rail lines hit again by sabotage attacks.
newsitem.headline: German rail lines hit again by sabotage attacks.

text.p: Unknown saboteurs disrupted several German rail lines early on Tuesday by throwing grappling hooks onto overhead power lines, the German rail Bundesbahn said.
There was no immediate indication who was responsible for the attacks which caused considerable damage. There were no reported injuries.
But anti-nuclear activists have tried to block rail traffic repeatedly in recent months to protest against a nuclear waste dumping ground in Gorleben northeast of Hanover.
Police said they suspect the attacks are linked to the transport of spent nuclear waste to Gorleben next week.

One train ran into one of the hooks near Frankfurt's International Airport just before 2 a.m. (0100 GMT). Traffic was being rerouted for several hours. Rail lines near Hamburg and Berlin were also hampered by similar attacks.

The medium-term nuclear storage site at Gorleben is a favourite target of the anti-nuclear movement. Last year violent protests took place and more than 19,000 police and border guards joined the biggest security operation in German peacetime history to get a shipment to the plant.
The latest delivery will include two rail containers from France and four more from German power plants, being moved at the same time to save costs for the required security operation.
